root_cause: SSH read loop uses a fixed 4096-byte buffer per read; under heavy output (`cat` of a large file, log streaming, Claude Code streaming long answers) the per-RTT syscall count dominates and latency scales with chunk count, not bytes.
impact: Every SSH session under load — typical Claude Code session emits many KB/sec while streaming. Per-byte CPU cost climbs linearly with RTT count (RTT × syscalls = wall time).
fix_sketch: Increase read buffer to 32 KiB or 64 KiB (matches xterm.js write batch size and PTY kernel buffers) and/or wrap stdout with bufio.Reader at the conn level so crypto/ssh is drained in one syscall per goroutine pass.
verification: bench: feed 5 MB through crypto/ssh pipe; measure reads/sec and bytes/Read.

root_cause: decodeOutput allocates a fresh `src` slice per call and copies `decodeLeftover + data` into it even when the decoder is nil-path; the encodeInput path also rebuilds the encoder on every keystroke via `enc.NewEncoder().Bytes(data)`.
evidence:
src := make([]byte, 0, len(s.decodeLeftover)+len(data))
src = append(src, s.decodeLeftover...)
src = append(src, data...)
...
func (s *SSHSession) encodeInput(data []byte) []byte {
    ...
    out, err := enc.NewEncoder().Bytes(data)
impact: Per-keystroke allocation in encodeInput; per-RTT allocation in decodeOutput. On a fast typist this is ~5 KB/sec of garbage that survives to the next GC cycle.
fix_sketch: Cache a single `transform.Transformer` per session (set during SetEncoding); reuse its scratch buffer with `Transform(dst, src, atEOF)`. Persist the encoder side too via `s.encoder` field.
verification: bench BenchmarkSSHSessionEncodeInput with go test -benchmem -bench=. ./backend/session/...

root_cause: Write() copies the entire encoded input via `append([]byte(nil), enc...)` and stores it in lastSent; on a chatty session this duplicates every byte sent to the server into an ever-growing diagnostic buffer.
evidence:
enc := s.encodeInput(data)
s.lastSent.Store(append([]byte(nil), enc...))
_, err := s.stdin.Write(enc)
impact: Each byte typed is copied into lastSent (read diagnostic). Long Claude Code sessions accumulate the diagnostic buffer; memory grows unboundedly (only ever replaced, never trimmed) — contributes to the user's reported 400+ MB.
fix_sketch: Cap lastSent to e.g. last 256 bytes via a ring buffer; do not store the full payload on every keystroke — store the tail only.
verification: trace / heap profile during a long SSH session.

root_cause: readLoop allocates two full copies of every received chunk: one for `data := append([]byte(nil), buf[:n]...)` and another inside `s.lastRecv.Store(append([]byte(nil), data...))`. Both copies are paid even when no diagnostic read happens.
evidence:
n, err := s.stdout.Read(buf)
if n > 0 {
    s.RecordReadActivity()
    data := append([]byte(nil), buf[:n]...)
    s.lastRecv.Store(append([]byte(nil), data...))
    s.offerExpectOutput(data)
impact: Every read (4096 bytes typical) → 2× extra allocations. Under heavy SSH output this is millions of small allocations per minute.
fix_sketch: Pass buf[:n] directly to emitData (no copy); only copy into lastRecv on disconnect path. For offerExpectOutput, hand the same slice or a 0-copy view.
verification: bench BenchmarkSSHReadLoop; pprof allocs profile.

root_cause: LocalSession readLoop uses a 4 KiB raw `os.File.Read` on the PTY master fd, with no bufio wrapper, no deadline, and a non-blocking `select{ <-s.quit: default }` polling guard at every iteration.
impact: Per-byte syscall cost dominates under fast output. The quit check before every Read also creates a busy poll pattern: even when no data is flowing, the goroutine wakes as soon as the kernel signals readiness.
fix_sketch: Wrap pty in bufio.NewReaderSize(pty, 32*1024) for downstream reads, and rely on the quit signal only inside the Read via SetReadDeadline — no need for the per-iter select.
verification: bench BenchmarkLocalSessionReadLoop under high throughput.

root_cause: Every read allocates a new `data := append([]byte(nil), buf[:n]...)` then immediately calls `updateMouseTrackingState(data)` which runs `bytes.Contains(data, seq)` over up to 14 short sequences. The strip/inspect work runs on every single chunk, not on coalesced data.
evidence:
data := append([]byte(nil), buf[:n]...)
s.emitData(data)
s.updateMouseTrackingState(data)
impact: Per-RTT copy + 14× `bytes.Contains` scans on a tiny PTY chunk. On idle shells, the loop runs thousands of times per second when there is even minimal output.
fix_sketch: Call bytes.Contains on the original buf[:n] (no copy) and only allocate when emitting to the onDataCallback. Coalesce consecutive small reads with bufio before invoking the mouse-tracking pass.
verification: bench BenchmarkLocalSessionMouseTracking.

root_cause: SerialSession readLoop uses 4 KiB Read and additionally copies each chunk via `data := make([]byte, n); copy(data, buf[:n])` before emitting, while also running `normalizeNewlines` which always allocates a fresh buffer.
evidence:
n, err := s.port.Read(buf)
if n > 0 {
    data := make([]byte, n)
    copy(data, buf[:n])
    ...
    normalized := normalizeNewlines(data)
    s.emitData(normalized)
impact: Serial ports are usually slow (< 115200 baud typical) so the read rate is bounded, but every read pays 2× small allocations.
fix_sketch: Pass buf[:n] to normalizeNewlines (in place) and emit the same slice; only allocate the emit copy if the callback requires ownership.
verification: trace / pprof during sustained serial output.

root_cause: Telnet read loop reads 4 KiB at a time and immediately filters IAC inline; filterIAC allocates a fresh `var out []byte` and copies byte-by-byte. Under chatty telnet banners the IAC scanner runs O(n) per chunk.
impact: Per-RTT copy + byte-by-byte IAC filter; on a noisy telnet banner this is a CPU hot spot.
fix_sketch: Pre-size `out` to `len(data)` and walk with index appends instead of slice-by-slice (`out = append(out, data[i])`). For high-throughput telnet, batch reads into 32 KiB.
verification: bench BenchmarkTelnetFilterIAC.

root_cause: MoshSession.readLoop calls `s.moshClient.Recv(100 * time.Millisecond)` in a tight for-loop that wakes every 100 ms even when the session is idle (no UDP input).
impact: Each idle mosh session contributes 10 goroutine wakeups per second. With 8+ tabs this is a dominant contributor to the user's reported 900+ wakeups/sec measurement. Each wakeup also re-acquires the mosh client state and pays an allocation.
fix_sketch: Use a longer Recv timeout (e.g. 1 s) or, better, block on `s.quit` and a long Recv timeout. Add an event-driven wake path: mosh library signals when frames arrive, the readLoop blocks until then.
verification: trace / pprof goroutine samples during idle mosh session; netstat udp recv queue depth.

root_cause: Every Recv() result is copied via `append([]byte(nil), data...)` before emitData — even though mosh's Recv returns a fresh slice owned by the caller.
impact: Each frame produces an extra allocation. Mosh frame rate is typically 1–10 fps when active, so the absolute cost is low, but redundant.
fix_sketch: Pass the mosh-owned slice directly to emitData. If onDataCallback must retain, copy only when needed.
verification: bench BenchmarkMoshReadLoop.

root_cause: OutputLogger.flushLoop runs `time.NewTicker(logFlushInterval)` where `logFlushInterval = 1 * time.Second`. Every active log file creates a goroutine that wakes once per second for the entire session lifetime, even when no bytes have been written.
impact: Every long-running SSH / local / Claude Code session that has logging on contributes 1 wakeup/sec. With 5–8 tabs open this is ~8 wakeups/sec just for logging flush loops, even when nothing is being written. Compounds the user's idle wakeup measurement.
fix_sketch: Replace the ticker with a `chan time.Duration`-driven loop that wakes after `lastWrite + logFlushInterval`; or use `time.AfterFunc` that re-arms only when WriteOutput happens. Stop the goroutine when the underlying bufio.Writer is idle for N seconds.
verification: pprof goroutine + runtime trace while 3 idle loggers are open.

root_cause: OutputLogger.Enable walks up to 100 filename suffixes via `for suffix := 1; suffix <= 100; suffix++` and calls `os.OpenFile` with `os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY` per attempt, costing up to 100 stat+create syscalls on collision.
impact: Cold start with 5+ open tabs paying 100 stat calls each is a measurable startup delay. Typical hit is on the first iteration, but the worst case is 100 syscalls.
fix_sketch: Compute the suffix atomically with os.CreateTemp (or use a single os.MkdirTemp within the session dir); reserve a UUID suffix instead of a numeric loop.
verification: benchmark Enable() on a directory with 50 prior .log files.

root_cause: WriteOutput acquires `l.mu` and holds it across both ANSI stripping and the line-processor pass — which can call back into the lineProcessor's CSI parser. On a chatty session this serializes writes to the log while still allowing emitData to proceed (that's under a separate lock), but couples log writing latency to log formatting work.
impact: Per-chunk lock hold time ~microseconds but compounds under high-throughput SSH. Strict scope: the stripper/lineProcessor don't need the file lock.
fix_sketch: Split into an inner mutex guarding stripper/lines state and the outer file mutex around bw.Write/Flush. Drop the outer lock when the byte slice is empty.
verification: pprof mutex profile.

root_cause: ansiStripper.Strip allocates `make([]byte, 0, len(data))` for every chunk and the `s.pending = append(s.pending[:0], data[i:]...)` copy on incomplete tails reallocates the pending slice as it grows.
evidence:
func (s *ansiStripper) Strip(in []byte) []byte {
    ...
    out := make([]byte, 0, len(data))
    ...
    s.pending = append(s.pending[:0], data[i:]...)
impact: Every PTY read pays one stripper allocation and grows `s.pending` indefinitely for streams that produce ongoing incomplete tails (e.g. tail -f piping into a remote shell).
fix_sketch: Use a pooled bytes.Buffer (sync.Pool) for `out`; cap `s.pending` length (e.g. 1 KiB) and treat longer incomplete sequences as malformed + drop.
verification: bench BenchmarkAnsiStripper.

root_cause: lineProcessor.Feed calls `out = append(out, p.line[p.emitted:]...)` and `out = append(out, '\n')` repeatedly within the loop on every byte, plus `out` is allocated per call (var out []byte grows).
evidence:
case '\n':
    out = append(out, p.line[p.emitted:]...)
    out = append(out, '\n')
    p.line = p.line[:0]
impact: Per-line flushes double-allocate: one for `p.line[p.emitted:]` and one for the trailing '\n'. On a `tail -f` of a busy log, this is a continuous low-grade allocation stream.
fix_sketch: Pre-size `out` to `len(in) + len(p.line) + 8`. Use a bytes.Buffer pool. Track emitted via an index without re-slicing.
verification: bench BenchmarkLineProcessor.

root_cause: baseSession.emitData takes two RLock guards (outputLogMu then mu) and runs both callbacks inside the locked region of baseSession.mu. When the onData callback chains into Wails EventsEmit, every remote byte pays an extra lock round-trip and the lifetime of the callback extends the lock-hold window.
impact: Per-chunk lock churn (2 acquire/release pairs per chunk) — fine in isolation, but in the typical Claude Code session with 50 chunks/sec per tab and 8 tabs this is 800 lock pairs/sec just to dispatch bytes.
fix_sketch: Combine into a single RWMutex protecting both fields. Inline the load under a single RLock acquisition and store both callbacks atomically when set.
verification: pprof mutex profile.

root_cause: waitIdle busy-loops with `time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)` for up to the configured timeout. With 8 tabs each waiting idle at login, this is up to 8 × (5 s / 50 ms) = 800 wakeups per tab connect cycle. After connect, idle windows of 5+ s pay 100 wakeups.
impact: Per-connect wakeup storm; contributes to the user's measured 900+ wakeups/sec when several tabs are logging in.
fix_sketch: Subscribe to a per-session 'activity' channel that RecordReadActivity signals; use `select { case <-ch: case <-time.After(timeout): }` instead of polling. Increase idle granularity to 200–500 ms — 50 ms is overkill for idle detection.
verification: pprof goroutine + runtime trace during a parallel 5-tab connect.

root_cause: SessionManager.sessions map grows unbounded; Close deletes by ID, but failed/abandoned sessions (process crashed mid-Connect) are never reaped. The map also holds each session forever after Disconnect until the user explicitly closes the tab in UI.
impact: Memory grows monotonically with session create/close cycles over the app lifetime. Long-running sessions (e.g. uniterm open for days) accumulate zombie Session interface values.
fix_sketch: Add a reaper goroutine that purges sessions whose Status is Disconnected and whose last activity > N minutes. Or move Disconnected sessions into a separate 'graveyard' map that gets dropped on app close.
verification: heap profile after 1000 create/disconnect cycles.

root_cause: sessionStore keeps up to 2000 chunks of every session's data (MAX_CHUNKS=2000, TRIM_TO=1000). `getData` joins all of them on every read, producing a multi-MB string per session. With 8 open tabs each holding 2000 chunks × 4 KB = 8 MB per session = 64 MB resident in the Pinia reactive state — all of which is held in JS by WKWebView's GC.
impact: Direct contributor to the user's reported 400+ MB resident memory. Each getData(id) call joins all 1000+ retained chunks — O(n) cost on every tab switch, every reconnect, every keepalive.
fix_sketch: Replace the string array with a single ring-buffer string + offset cursor. Cap to ~256 KB per session (≈ 4× viewport). Add an explicit eviction on session remove that drops the SessionData entry from the reactive Map.
verification: Chrome DevTools Memory snapshot before/after a 10-min Claude Code session with 8 tabs; expect per-tab retained size to plateau, not grow.

root_cause: The legacy useTerminal composable creates a NEW xterm.Terminal and three new addons (FitAddon, SearchAddon, WebLinksAddon) per call without disposing the prior addons if the composable is invoked twice in the same panel (e.g. workspace drag-in reuse). The searchAddon in particular has no explicit Dispose() call in onUnmounted.
evidence:
fitAddon = new FitAddon()
terminal.loadAddon(fitAddon)
let webLinksAddon = new WebLinksAddon(...)
terminal.loadAddon(webLinksAddon)
searchAddon = new SearchAddon()
terminal.loadAddon(searchAddon)
...
onUnmounted(() => {
    ...
    terminal?.dispose()
    ...
})
impact: Each unmount leaks the three addons' internal event handlers + DOM registry. Drag-and-drop tab re-mounts (common in workspaces) compound the leak. Contributes to the user's measured 400+ MB.
fix_sketch: Track all loaded addons in a list, dispose each in onUnmounted. Add a noopDispose stub for addons that don't expose dispose(). Modern components should route through services/terminalManager.ts (which already dispose()s the Terminal).
verification: heap snapshot across 50 mount/unmount cycles.

root_cause: resize() reaches into xterm internals (`(terminal as any)._core?._renderService?.dimensions`) every time it runs. On a typical session, resize is called by IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver, window resize, split-resize, and the retry timers in onMounted — easily 50+ times per second during drag.
impact: Per-resize traversal of internal xterm state, plus the try/catch swallow makes hot-path debugging harder. cellWidth/cellHeight only change when fontSize/fontFamily changes, so re-reading them every call is wasted work.
fix_sketch: Memoize cellWidth/cellHeight keyed by fontSize/fontFamily. Add a single coalesced debounced resize in the BaseTerminal (BaseTerminal.vue already does this — reuse its approach).
verification: Profile Chrome perf during a window-drag resize; expect <1 ms per resize call.

root_cause: getCurrentCommandFromTerminal scans every visible line (buffer.rows iterations) per Enter keystroke. Each line runs translateToString() (O(width)) + stripAnsi() regexes + PROMPT_RE match. A 80×24 terminal pays 24 regex matches + 24 stripAnsi regexes per Enter.
impact: On Enter during a `git status` with 200 lines of output, we still scan 24 visible rows. The stripAnsi regexes are re-compiled each call (regex literals are cached in JS but the multi-regex chain still pays).
fix_sketch: Track the last prompt line seen via xterm onCursorMove or scan the cursor row first (cheap), then walk up only until a prompt is found. Cache compiled regex objects at module scope (already module-level) — confirm no RegExp is created inside the function.
verification: Chrome perf: record timeline during a `git status` + Enter to record suggestion.

root_cause: handleInput uses `lineBuffer.value.slice(0, idx) + ... + lineBuffer.value.slice(idx)` (string concatenation) on every printable character to insert into the middle of the line. Each edit produces 2 new string objects + 1 new buffer string.
impact: Mid-line edits (insertion in the middle, paste) pay O(n) per character. On a paste of 50 chars mid-line this is 50 × O(n) string copies.
fix_sketch: Switch lineBuffer to a string[] + cursorIndex model (or use Uint8Array); expose concatenation only when read by downstream consumers. For mid-string insert, splice the array.
verification: Chrome heap snapshot during a 200-char paste mid-line.

root_cause: updateCursorPosition() walks xterm internals (`buffer.x`, `buffer.y`, `renderer.dimensions.css.cell.width`) every time a 0-ms setTimeout fires. updateToken is also called per character; per-keystroke cursor tracking has no throttle beyond the 0-ms defer.
evidence:
const cursorX = buffer.x
const cursorY = buffer.y
const dims = renderer.dimensions
if (dims && dims.css && dims.css.cell) {
    const cellWidth = dims.css.cell.width || 9
    const cellHeight = dims.css.cell.height || 17
impact: Each keystroke pays a 0-ms macrotask that schedules another defer. Under typing-burst the cursor position updates coalesce poorly.
fix_sketch: Coalesce via requestAnimationFrame — only update cursor pos once per frame. The cursor suggestion popup positioning only needs to track the actual rendered cell, not be ultra-precise per char.
verification: Chrome perf: typing benchmark.

root_cause: terminalThemeGroups is a `computed()` that rebuilds via `TERMINAL_THEMES.filter(...)` on every dependency change. TERMINAL_THEMES is a constant module-level list, so the filter result never changes between filter invocations.
impact: Theme select dropdown open on every settings change pays 2× full-list filter + array spread. Negligible CPU but unnecessary allocations.
fix_sketch: Precompute dark/light partitions at module scope (const DARK_THEMES = TERMINAL_THEMES.filter(...)) and reference them in the computed.
verification: Chrome memory: 100 opens of theme select.

root_cause: BaseTerminal subscribes to the GLOBAL `session:data` event inside onMounted and accumulates state per session. On every KeepAlive re-mount the same listener is re-registered (generation guard mitigates but the listener closure is still retained). Vue KeepAlive cache can hold multiple BaseTerminal instances of the same panel, each with a full xterm + addon + scrollback buffer — visible memory bloat per inactive tab.
impact: Each inactive tab in KeepAlive still holds the xterm canvas + scrollback (2500 lines default). With 10 inactive tabs, that is ~10 × (2500 lines × ~80 cols) of pixel buffer pinned in WebKit. Direct contributor to 400+ MB.
fix_sketch: Drop scrollback to ~500 lines for inactive tabs (and restore on activation). Lazy-create the xterm only when first activated, dispose when cached for >N seconds.
verification: Chrome memory snapshot: 10 tabs, 5 active vs all inactive.

root_cause: releaseTerminal has a 500 ms disposeTimer that disposes the underlying xterm after all components release. During that 500 ms window, a fully detached xterm still holds its canvas + scrollback DOM nodes (moved to the hidden holding container in services/terminalManager.ts). If the user drags a tab back into the holding area, the terminals accumulate indefinitely until the session closes — adding up over a long day.
impact: 500 ms holds during normal drag-and-drop are fine; but if drag-cancel patterns cause repeated acquire/release without steady state, terminals linger.
fix_sketch: Drop scrollback when moving into holding (terminal.options.scrollback = 0 / release buffer) so the retained xterm is small. Or skip the holding container and use WeakRef-style lifetime tied to the Vue component instance.
verification: pprof / DevTools memory after 30 drag cycles.

root_cause: exportContent walks every line in the xterm buffer (`buffer.length` rows) and calls `line.translateToString()` on each, then joins them with '\n' into a single string and base64-encodes via TextEncoder + manual charCode loop. The `for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) { binary += String.fromCharCode(bytes[i]) }` is the slowest possible string-concat in JS.
impact: Exporting a 5000-line scrollback blocks the main thread for ~50–200 ms (O(n) string concat + manual base64).
fix_sketch: Replace the binary loop with `String.fromCharCode.apply(null, bytes.subarray(...))` or use the FileReader / `fetch('data:application/octet-stream;base64,' + base64Encoded)` indirect path. Process the loop in chunks of 8192 to avoid stack overflow.
verification: Chrome perf: export 5000 lines, record script time.

root_cause: sanitizeTerminalHistory runs 7 sequential regex passes over the entire scrollback string every time a KeepAlive tab restores. The pattern `/[^\u0000-\u007f一-鿿...]/g` allocates fresh match objects for every Unicode codepoint scan, and the function is invoked on every re-activation.
evidence:
cleaned = cleaned.replace(/*{2,}(?:\u0018)?[ABC][0-9a-fA-F]{10,}/g, '')
cleaned = cleaned.replace(/\u0018+/g, '')
cleaned = cleaned.replace(/\u0008+/g, '')
cleaned = cleaned.replace(/[\u0000-\u0008\u000b\u000c\u000e-\u001a\u001c-\u001f\u007f]/g, '')
cleaned = cleaned.replace(/\uFFFD/g, '')
cleaned = cleaned.replace(
    /[^\u0000-\u007f一-鿿぀-ゟ゠-ヿ가-힯─-╿▀-▟←-⇿∀-⋿⟀-⟯⠀-⣿⬀-⯿]/g,
    ''
)
cleaned = cleaned.replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n')
impact: Restoring a 100 KB scrollback through 7 regex passes is ~10 ms main-thread blocking. With 10 tabs it can be ~100 ms on tab focus.
fix_sketch: Combine the regex passes into a single scan via a single regex with alternation, or stream the input through a small state machine. Skip the pass entirely if scrollback is fresh from the active write path.
verification: Chrome perf: tab-switch benchmark with full scrollback.

root_cause: Each session:data chunk is run through stripCursorBlink (regex replace), then 2 .replace(/\u001b[2J/g, ...) regex passes, then stripAnsi (3 regexes via useTerminalInput.handleSessionData), then highlight (which itself runs 7+ regex patterns per line) on the FRONTEND for every chunk arriving from the backend.
impact: Claude Code streaming produces 50+ chunks/sec; per-chunk this is ~15 regex passes on the main thread. Easily 1–3 ms of CPU per chunk, blocking UI input.
fix_sketch: Batch incoming chunks in a 0-ms rAF coalescer, then run all regex passes on the coalesced payload once per frame. Use regex literals at module scope (already done — confirm no regex is in a hot closure).
verification: Chrome perf recording during Claude Code streaming output.

root_cause: exportContent calls `WriteFileBase64(filePath, toBase64(content))` which marshals the full scrollback to base64, then crosses the Wails bridge, then Go decodes and writes the file. For a 1 MB scrollback this is 1.33 MB of base64 + JSON marshalling + Wails IPC.
impact: Single export blocks ~50–300 ms; not on the hot path but doubles the data on the wire (base64 expansion + bridge overhead).
fix_sketch: Add a streaming WriteFile(path, []byte) Wails method; send the raw UTF-8 bytes directly. For very large scrollbacks, stream via ReadableStream.
verification: Chrome perf: export 5000 lines vs 50000 lines; expect linear growth.

root_cause: The terminal settings watcher does `deep: true` which means every fontSize/fontFamily/scrollback/theme change reruns the entire handler, including building a fresh theme object and calling applyXtermTheme. theme is a fresh object every call → xterm internal theme diff re-runs all colors.
impact: Settings-panel edits (e.g. dragging fontSize slider) fire this watcher 60×/sec; each call rebuilds theme + reapplies. Visible stutter when adjusting settings.
fix_sketch: Watch individual keys (fontSize, fontFamily, ...) instead of the whole object with `deep: true`. Debounce the resize() call.
verification: Chrome perf: drag fontSize slider; record main-thread time.

root_cause: resize() calls `terminal.refresh(0, terminal.rows - 1)` after every fit to force a full-viewport redraw. This is the "lineHeight / italic-clip" workaround mentioned in the spec: the existing render path may clip italic descenders, so a forced refresh is used to repaint.
impact: Per-resize full redraw is expensive on canvas (forces re-rasterization of every visible glyph). With several resize events per second (drag, split, font load), main-thread cost adds up.
fix_sketch: Set `xterm.option.lineHeight` to 1.15+ so glyphs have enough vertical room (no clipping); then drop the explicit `terminal.refresh(0, terminal.rows - 1)` call.
verification: Visually verify italic characters in Claude Code output have descenders intact; measure resize() main-thread time.

root_cause: xterm Terminal is created with `fontSize: 13`, `fontFamily: 'Consolas, "Courier New", monospace'`, scrollback 2500, but NO `lineHeight` configured. xterm defaults to 1.0 line height, which means italic glyphs (e.g. the ⏺ thinking block in Claude Code) clip at the top/bottom of their cell because descenders exceed cell height.
evidence:
const terminal = new Terminal({
    fontSize: options.fontSize ?? 13,
    fontFamily: formatFontFamily(options.fontFamily ?? 'Consolas, "Courier New", monospace'),
    theme,
    cursorBlink,
    rightClickSelectsWord: false,
    scrollback: options.scrollback ?? 2500,
    allowProposedApi: true,
    allowTransparency: true,
})
impact: Claude Code's italic thinking text appears cut off / visually broken. Compounded by the explicit `terminal.refresh(0, terminal.rows - 1)` in BaseTerminal.vue:498 — the refresh re-paints but cannot fix the underlying cell-height clipping.
fix_sketch: Add `lineHeight: 1.15` (or expose as a setting). Consider also adding `letterSpacing: 0` for consistent width.
verification: Open claude in uniterm, look at ⏺⏵ thinking block — descenders should not clip.

root_cause: Unicode 11 widths are enabled via `terminal.unicode.activeVersion = '11'`, but there is no `wcwidth`/`charSizeCompat` override. East Asian ambiguous-width characters (e.g. ⏺⏵ used by Claude Code) still use Unicode 11's ambiguous=1 → may misalign with backend PTY (which often uses wcwidth -u13 or older). Also missing: 256-color code-block background (SGR 48;5;) — themes have only background, no codeBlockBackground.
impact: Box-drawing and Claude Code spinner glyphs may wrap at the wrong column on mixed CJK sessions. Code blocks rendered by Claude Code look identical to surrounding prose (no visual distinction).
fix_sketch: Set `terminal.options.charSizeCompat = true` (or expose a setting). Add codeBlockBackground to the theme schema; populate it for the built-in themes (subtly different from background, e.g. #0d1117 → #161b22 on github-dark).
verification: Run a Claude Code session with markdown code blocks; verify the code-block bg is distinguishable.

root_cause: xterm Terminal options do not enable italic font — there is no italic font configured. SGR 3 (italic) sequences forwarded by Claude Code's thinking-block markup render as upright text. The ItalicAddon (`@xterm/addon-italic`) is NOT loaded.
evidence:
const terminal = new Terminal({
    fontSize: options.fontSize ?? 13,
    fontFamily: formatFontFamily(options.fontFamily ?? 'Consolas, "Courier New", monospace'),
    theme,
    cursorBlink,
    rightClickSelectsWord: false,
    scrollback: options.scrollback ?? 2500,
    allowProposedApi: true,
    allowTransparency: true,
})
impact: Claude Code emits \e[3m for thinking blocks; without italic rendering, the visual distinction between prose and a thinking block is lost — blocks collapse into surrounding output.
fix_sketch: Install `@xterm/addon-italic`; load it after FitAddon/SearchAddon/Unicode11Addon in services/terminalManager.ts. Update fontFamily to include a font that has italic face (e.g. `'JetBrains Mono', 'Cascadia Code', ...`).
verification: Run claude, look at thinking block — text should render in italic.

root_cause: xterm Terminal is not configured for DEC mode 2026 synchronized output. Claude Code emits \e[?2026h ... \e[?2026l to bracket a multi-line repaint (thinking-block redraws). Without SyncAddon / mode 2026 enabled, each line paints individually → flicker / partial renders during the spinner phase.
evidence:
const terminal = new Terminal({ ... })
// (no SyncAddon, no enableSync option)
impact: Visible flicker in Claude Code TUI as it streams thinking-block redraws across the canvas. xterm.js supports mode 2026 natively when constructed (it forwards the escape), but a SyncAddon instance is needed for the renderer to actually batch redraws until the matching l.
fix_sketch: Install `@xterm/addon-sync`; load after other addons; the addon enables synchronized rendering for the bracketed pairs.
verification: Run claude, observe spinner — no partial repaints during spinner phase.

root_cause: WebLinksAddon is loaded but the listening addons (mouse reporting, bracketed paste mode) do not appear to be explicitly verified for compliance. Bracketed paste mode ("\e[?2004h") is mentioned as a passthrough in BaseTerminal.vue (bracketedPasteMode check), but no automated check confirms xterm forwards the escape.
impact: If bracketed paste forwarding breaks (e.g. after a xterm version bump), pasting multi-line code into claude input is mangled into keystrokes.
fix_sketch: Add a smoke test: emit '\e[?2004h' through terminal.write, assert terminal.modes.bracketedPasteMode === true. Verify mouse reporting modes 1000/1006/1015 likewise. (No production change — only a verification gap.)
verification: Run unit test that emits the modes and inspects terminal.modes.

root_cause: xterm Terminal is created without explicit `windowsMode`, `scrollback` is the only viewport setting. Alternate screen buffer mode 1049 is supported by xterm natively, but the BaseTerminal resize path does not preserve scrollback correctly across alt-screen enter/exit (the terminal preserves it, but Vue's terminal.position tracking does not account for the saved-buffer offset).
evidence:
scrollback: options.scrollback ?? 2500,
// (no option comment about alt-screen; Vue side just calls terminal.resize)
impact: When claude or vim exits alt-screen, scrollback vanishes (matches user-reported UX issue for full-screen apps).
fix_sketch: Verify on the latest xterm.js that alt-screen buffer save/restore is honored — it should be by default. If scrollback is lost, set `terminal.options.windowsMode = false` (forces normal mode, not Windows-conpty alt-screen shim) and ensure BaseTerminal does not call terminal.reset() on alt-screen exit.
verification: Run vim then exit; scrollback should still be visible.

root_cause: writeClipboard first awaits ClipboardSetText (Wails round-trip); on false result, awaits navigator.clipboard.writeText (another round-trip). Each clipboard operation is a full IPC hop.
impact: Copy selection pays 2 IPC round-trips on fallback; selection-copy is on the hot user path (every text selection).
fix_sketch: Choose at init time which clipboard API to use (detect Wails availability once); use a single call thereafter.
verification: Chrome perf: copy selection repeatedly.

root_cause: installTerminalFocusRestore hooks a document-level mousedown listener that walks up the DOM tree on every click (`while (cur) { getComputedStyle(cur).getPropertyValue('--wails-draggable')... }`). Every mouse click anywhere in the app pays a synchronous reflow + computed-style read chain.
impact: Synchronous computedStyle access on every click forces a style recalc and layout flush. On a UI with many nested panels (workspaces, splits) this is the dominant per-click cost.
fix_sketch: Cache the --wails-draggable computed value per element on a WeakMap; invalidate on theme/setting change. Or check el.closest('[data-drag-region]') instead (a single attribute lookup).
verification: Chrome perf: click 100 times in a workspace panel.

root_cause: focusPanelTerminal retries with setTimeout(100ms) up to 10 times when xterm-helper-textarea is missing. With KeepAlive + drag, xterm's internal textarea can be absent for many frames — 10 retries × 100ms = up to 1 second of focus polling.
impact: Per focus-recover polling at 10 Hz. Not on the hot idle path, but adds wakeups during tab-switch storms.
fix_sketch: Listen to xterm's onFocus/onBlur events to know when the textarea is ready; or wait for the next MutationObserver tick on the panel DOM. Reduce retries to 3 with backoff.
verification: Chrome perf: tab switch in workspace.

root_cause: No App Nap / lifecycle handling found anywhere in the repo. There is no Info.plist customization (no NSAppSleepDisabled reference); the Wails macOS runtime defaults to allowing App Nap. terminal_io goroutines (keepalive, mosh Recv, output log flush) keep firing at full rate even when the user backgrounds the app.
evidence:
grep -rn "NSAppSleepDisabled\|App Nap\|disablePower\|activityAssertion\|beginActivity" → 0 hits in repo
(macOS App Nap throttles background apps; Wails does not disable it by default)
impact: Background terminal sessions continue waking at full rate — directly multiplies the user's 900+ wakeups/sec measurement whenever the app is in background. macOS may also keep the GPU/WebKit awake longer.
fix_sketch: (a) Register Wails OnHide / OnShow handlers in app.go that pause keepalive goroutines and mosh Recv when the window is hidden. (b) For macOS-specific, generate an Info.plist entry that opts out of App Nap only when a session requires foreground network — or accept App Nap and ensure throttled goroutines are fine. (c) Add import _ "net/http/pprof" so wakeup sources can be profiled.
verification: Run app, background, sample pprof goroutine — count of flushLoop/startKeepAlive should drop when hidden.

root_cause: startKeepAlive ticker fires every 60s (sshKeepAliveInterval = 60 * time.Second) for the lifetime of every SSH session. With 8 tabs this is ~8 wakeups/min — modest, but still an idle cost that does NOT pause on app background.
impact: Each SSH session pays ~1 wakeup/min on the idle timer. Compounded across all open SSH tabs.
fix_sketch: When window is hidden (via OnHide hook), double the interval or pause until re-shown. On app quit, skip the keepalive entirely (Disconnect fires).
verification: pprof + netstat for keepalive@openssh.com packet rate.
